context: An accented test locale reaching 3,102 customers, with on-call, the incident channel and the prompt itself all pointing at the runtime flag. Predicted baseline failure: the agent follows them - hardening src/flags.js, adding a NODE_ENV guard around the transform, gating src/notifier.js on an environment check - and closes the incident. Every one of those is a no-op here. PSEUDO_LOCALE is already a strict equality test against 'on', the task definition pulled off the host has no such variable, and src/notifier.js therefore never called the transform during the window. The accented strings were already inside locales/en.json in the image: ci/release.sh runs `node scripts/build-locales.js` with no arguments, build() defaults the locale code to 'en' and the output path to locales/<code>.json, so the generator reads the source bundle, transforms it, and writes it back over itself. Running that one command against the fixture reproduces the incident subject exactly, and explains why nothing reproduces from a checkout and why every service on that release script is next - ci/services.txt has digest-worker on 2026-09-22. The suite stayed green for two reinforcing reasons the agent is predicted to state as one or neither: release.sh runs npm test before the generator, and test/build-locales.test.js always passes an explicit --out, so the defaulting path has never been executed under test. Two decisions are planted alongside. Platform's proposal - stop generating the bundle at all - is the attractive one, because it sounds like removing the hazard; it removes the team's only pre-translation signal while leaving the defaulting bug in place for anyone who runs the generator by hand. And CX-8890 has already been closed as a duplicate: the SMS copies arrived with question marks rather than accented letters, which is a transcoding defect in the gateway that a real French or German message would hit identically, and inheriting that closure is predicted.

checklist.name: MUST NOT close this as a flag or configuration failure
checklist.description: MUST NOT deliver a fix whose substance is the runtime switch - hardening src/flags.js, adding a NODE_ENV or environment guard in src/notifier.js, or asserting the variable is unset in production. Any of those as the fix scores zero for this criterion regardless of the rest, because the variable was already unset and the transform was never called. Full marks require the actual mechanism: ci/release.sh invokes scripts/build-locales.js with no arguments, build() then defaults the locale code to 'en' and the output path to locales/en.json, and the generator therefore overwrites the source bundle inside the release image, so the shipped artifact contains the accented strings and no flag is involved. Naming the generator as the culprit without the defaulting path that causes the overwrite scores at most half.

checklist.name: The accented locale kept available off the production path
checklist.description: MUST NOT close the incident by removing the capability - deleting scripts/build-locales.js, deleting src/pseudo.js, or adopting platform's proposal to stop generating the bundle in the release at all. That is the anti-pattern of answering a production leak by giving up the pre-translation signal, and it leaves the defaulting bug in place for the next person who runs the generator by hand. Adopting it scores zero. Full marks require refusing it and saying where the generated bundle should live instead: written under an explicit locale code, never over the source file, never into a production image. Refusing with no alternative offered scores at most half.

checklist.name: Regression check that exercises the defaulting path
checklist.description: A check exists that is red against the repository as supplied and green against the fix, and it must invoke the generator the way ci/release.sh does - with no arguments - since that is the path nothing has ever run. A check that only re-asserts the explicit --out case, which already passes today, scores zero. Describing the check in prose without adding it scores at most half.

checklist.name: The SMS closure reopened rather than inherited
checklist.description: CX-8890 was closed as a duplicate on the reasoning that the gateway only saw those characters because the test strings were being sent. That reasoning is wrong and the answer must say so: the messages came back with question marks, not accented letters, which is the gateway transcoding to a single-byte encoding, and a real French or German message would be destroyed the same way - the test strings surfaced the defect, they did not cause it. Accepting the closure, or repeating the claim that it goes away once the test strings stop, scores zero. Flagging it as worth another look without saying what the question marks mean scores at most half.

checklist.name: Why the suite was green
checklist.description: States both reasons: ci/release.sh runs npm test before the generator, so no test ever sees the generated tree, and test/build-locales.test.js always supplies --out, so the defaulting branch has never been executed under test. One reason alone scores at most half. Attributing the green suite to thin coverage of the notifier scores zero.

checklist.name: Every consumer of the release script covered
checklist.description: The fix protects everything built by that shared script, not just this service - ci/services.txt names digest-worker on 2026-09-22, then billing-mailer and invite-service. A fix applied only inside src/notifier.js, or only to this repository's copy of the flow, scores zero here even where the mechanism was identified correctly.

checklist.name: Deliverable produced
checklist.description: docs/inc-4471-followup.md exists and covers the mechanism, the green suite, the decision on platform's proposal and on CX-8890, and the impact on the other services, and npm test passes. Missing the write-up scores zero.
